page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Marginal notes in the left margin, beside lines 1, 4, 6, 7-8, 11, 13, 14 and 15. Running head at top, page number at top left. Catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: Iudith 6.citor in castra Hebræorum jubet, ut cum his periret, quos vinci non posse affirmaverat. At tum Iudæi montes petiverant, ita quibus id negotii datum, ima montiū successere, ibiq; vinctum Accitor reliquerunt. Quod ubi Iudæi animadverterūt, ex-aBethuliaemptum vinculis in {a}collem perducunt. Caufas rei quærentibus, gesta exponit, receptusq; parem exitum operiebatur. Is post victoriam circumcisus, {b}Iudæus factus est. b Achiorfacra In-deorum suscipit.Igitur Holofernes difficultate locorum comperta, quia adiri præcelsa non poterant, montes militibus circundat, & summa cura Hebræos aquationibus prohibet: eoque maturius obsidionem sense-re, Itaque victi penuria aquæ, ad Oziam Iudith 7.principem concurrunt, proni omnes ad deditionem. Ille vero opperiendum paulisper, & divinum auxilium exspectandum respondens, {c}quintodecimo die deditionis tempus constituit. Quod ubi Iudith compertum, quæ viro vidua, prædiues opibus, insignis specie, sed moribus quam vultu illustrior, tum in castris erat, arctis suorum rebus, etiam certo sibi exitio audendum aliquid & tentandum rata, caput comit, vultu expolitur, comite ancilla castra

page.notes: Notes at the foot are my own sorting of the marginal notes; the margin reads "Iudith 6.", "aBethulia", "b Achior", "facra In-" "deorum" "suscipit.", "Iudith 7.", "c quinto", "est Iud. 7.23" and "intexta Graeco". Uncertain readings: "fense-re" written as "sense-re" (the hyphenated word at the line end is doubtful); "montiū" and "succefsere" (the scan is faint and the letters around the s are uncertain); "comite ancilla" at the end of the last line. The page-end catchword "castra" is the first word of the next page. Long s is written as plain s throughout.
